overview.short: Takht Sri Harmandir Ji Patna Sahib is one of the five holy Takhts of Sikhism, marking the birthplace of the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh Ji, in 1666 CE.
overview.description: Nestled on the banks of the sacred River Ganga in the historic quarters of Patna City (Patliputra), Takht Sri Patna Sahib is an internationally revered spiritual sanctuary. Originally constructed by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the 19th century and rebuilt in pristine white marble, the shrine preserves priceless Sikh relics including Guru Gobind Singh Ji’s golden cradles, childhood weapons (Talwar & Khanjar), the sacred Guru Granth Sahib handwritten with golden inks, and footprints of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.
features: One of the Five Holy Takhts of Sikhism
Priceless Relics of Guru Gobind Singh Ji
Historic Gurdwara Circuit along the Ganga
overview.about: A monumental spiritual center vibrating with round-the-clock Gurbani kirtan, compassionate langar service, and rich seventeenth-century Sikh heritage along the holy Ganga.

howToReach.roadNote: Located in Patna City, easily reached via Ashok Rajpath, Patna Marine Drive (Ganga Path), and NH-31.

routes.byTrain: Vande Bharat / Rajdhani to Patna (8 hrs)

topPlaces.name: Takht Sri Harmandir Ji Main Sanctum
topPlaces.description: Magnificent white marble Takht sanctum housing the sacred relics, gilded arches, and continuous Gurbani Kirtan echoing through the main darbar hall.

image.alt: Takht Sri Harmandir Ji Main Sanctum in Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Gurdwara Bal Lila Maini Sangat
topPlaces.description: Historic palace of Raja Fateh Chand Maini where child Gobind Rai played, famous for its tradition of serving boiled gram (Chhola-Poori) in memory of Rani Maini.

image.alt: Gurdwara Bal Lila Maini Sangat in Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Gurdwara Guru Ka Bagh
topPlaces.description: Lush historic garden site where Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji rested on his return from Assam, causing the dry garden of Nawab Rahim Bakhsh to bloom miraculously.

image.alt: Gurdwara Guru Ka Bagh in Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Gurdwara Gai Ghat (Bhai Jaita Ji Shrine)
topPlaces.description: Sacred riverfront shrine where Guru Nanak Dev Ji sanctified the residence of devout disciple Bhai Jetha Ji on his First Udasi in the early 16th century.

image.alt: Gurdwara Gai Ghat (Bhai Jaita Ji Shrine) - Hukamnama of Guru Hargobind issued to the Purab di Sangat (congregation). Thi

topPlaces.name: Bihar Museum (World-Class Heritage Galleries)
topPlaces.description: State-of-the-art international museum designed by Maki & Associates, showcasing the Didarganj Yakshi (3rd century BCE), Mauryan relics, and 3,000 years of Bihar history.

image.alt: Bihar Museum (World-Class Heritage Galleries) in Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Golghar Granary & Ganga Viewpoint
topPlaces.description: Iconic beehive-shaped stupa-style granary built in 1786 by Captain John Garstin, featuring twin spiraling staircases offering panoramic views of Patna and the River Ganga.

image.alt: Golghar Granary & Ganga Viewpoint in Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Buddha Smriti Park & Karuna Stupa
topPlaces.description: Serene 22-acre urban memorial park housing the 200-foot Patliputra Karuna Stupa with authentic holy Buddha relics and sapling planted by the Dalai Lama.

image.alt: Buddha Smriti Park & Karuna Stupa in Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Sabhyata Dwar & Ganga Path Marine Drive
topPlaces.description: Monumental 32-meter red and white sandstone archway celebrating ancient Mauryan civilizational glory along the vibrant Ganga riverfront promenade.

image.alt: Sabhyata Dwar & Ganga Path Marine Drive in Takht Sri Patna Sahib, Bihar

faq.q: Is accommodation available at Takht Sri Patna Sahib for pilgrims?
faq.a: Yes, Guru Gobind Singh Ji Niwas and several large Yatri Niwas complexes provide clean, modern rooms and dormitories for pilgrims.

faq.q: What is the dress code for entering Takht Sri Patna Sahib?
faq.a: Heads must be covered with a scarf or turban (provided at the entrance), shoes deposited at the shoe counter, and feet washed at the water trough.

faq.q: How can visitors view the sacred weapons and relics of Guru Gobind Singh Ji?
faq.a: The sacred relics (weapons, cradle, and manuscripts) are displayed for public darshan twice daily during the special relic display ceremony.
